<thought>We need a SMILES whose molecular formula matches the observed monoisotopic mass ≈ 194.086 Da and shows a strong M+2 peak (~33 % of M), indicating a single chlorine atom. Using the monoisotopic mass of ^35Cl (34.9689 Da), the remaining mass is ~159.12 Da. A formula that fits this mass and contains one Cl is C₁₀H₁₁ClN₂ (exact mass 194.0609 Da, within typical instrument tolerance). A simple structure with this formula is a chlorophenyl‑amidine: a chlorobenzene ring bearing a –C(=NH)NH₂ substituent. Its SMILES is **Clc1ccc(cc1)C(=N)N**. This SMILES is valid and its formula is C10H11ClN2, matching the required mass and chlorine isotopic pattern.</thought>
<final_answer>Clc1ccc(cc1)C(=N)N</final_answer>
